registers.impact_note: Say what this does to scope, cost, time and quality. Leave a field blank if you genuinely do not know — a zero you do not mean understates the change at the moment somebody approves it.
registers.realise_note: The risk stays on the register as realised, and the new issue points back at it — that link is the evidence somebody saw this coming.
registers.confirm_submit_body: {code} goes to whoever approves changes on this project. You will not be able to edit it while it is with them.
registers.confirm_implement_title: Apply this change to the plan?
registers.confirm_implement_body: {code} is applied and a baseline is taken, so its effect on the schedule stays measurable afterwards.
registers.close_needs_note: Say why the risk is being closed.
registers.needs_root_cause: An incident or critical issue has to record its root cause.
registers.change_not_editable: That change request is with an approver.
registers.change_not_approved: Only an approved change can be applied.
registers.no_flow_auto: No approval flow is designed for change requests on this workspace, so it was recorded as approved.

portfolio.title: Portfolio
portfolio.subtitle: Programmes and projects, and what they are spending against.
portfolio.portfolio_hint: A set of programmes and projects competing for the same money.
portfolio.programme_hint: A set of projects delivering one outcome together.
portfolio.empty_body: A programme is a set of projects delivering one outcome — a hospital's building, IT and staffing. A portfolio is a set of programmes and projects competing for the same money. Both are optional: if you run unrelated jobs, you do not need either.
portfolio.no_projects: No projects in this programme yet.
portfolio.unassigned_sub: Shown so the rollup above is not quietly missing them.
portfolio.budget_hint: What this portfolio may spend. Without it there is nothing to compare against.
portfolio.outcome_hint: One sentence. A programme without a single outcome is a portfolio under another name.
portfolio.assign_note: A project in a programme takes that programme's portfolio automatically — two answers to “which portfolio” is how a rollup stops adding up.

templates.title: Project templates
templates.subtitle: What a new project can start from, so the parts people forget are already there.
templates.capture: Capture a project as a template
templates.capture_sub: Turn a job that went well into a starting point for the next one.
templates.capture_note: Dates are stored as offsets from the project's start, never as calendar dates — a template with real dates is correct on the day it is written and wrong every day after.
templates.none_hint: Capture a project that went well, and the next one starts from it.
templates.sub_type_hint: Residential, roads, ERP, campaign — whatever people call it.
templates.confirm_remove_body: {name} will no longer be offered. Projects created from it are untouched.
templates.confirm_hide_body: {name} is a shipped template, so it is hidden rather than deleted — a delete would come back on the next upgrade.
templates.start_from_sub: This project has no plan yet, so one can be laid over it.

gates.title: Stage gates
gates.subtitle: What has to be true before this project moves on.
gates.criteria_hint: Written before the decision, not after it.
gates.waiver_needs_reason: A waived gate has to say why. Skipping one without a reason is the record being deleted in slow motion.
gates.none_hint: Without one, a stage is a label somebody changes.

site_records.title: Site records
site_records.subtitle: Instructions, tests, inspections and completion — the paper a claim is argued from.
site_records.instructions_sub: What you were told to do, when, and by whom
site_records.tests_sub: Samples taken, and what the lab said
site_records.inspections_sub: “Come and look before I cover this up”
site_records.completion_sub: Practical, sectional and final — the certificates that release retention
site_records.unconverted_title: {count} instruction(s) claimed as a variation but never raised as one
site_records.unconverted_body: This is where money goes missing on a final account. Raise them, or clear the claim.
site_records.no_instructions_hint: “You told us to” is only an argument if there is a reference and a date.
site_records.no_inspections_hint: Missing one is what turns finished work into work that has to be opened again.
site_records.no_completion_hint: Practical completion starts the defects period and usually releases half the retention.
site_records.issued_by_hint: The engineer or client representative — usually not somebody with a login here.
site_records.field_instruction: What you were told to do
site_records.variation_hint: Record your view now, not months later when the account is argued.
site_records.instruction_sub: Filed before anybody agrees whether it is a variation — that is the point of it.
site_records.element_hint: “Ground floor slab, bay 3” — enough to find it again.
site_records.fail_raises_ncr: A failed test raises a non-conformance automatically. The pour it came from is already buried, so this is not left to somebody to remember.
site_records.requested_for_hint: An inspection wanted this afternoon is not a notice.
site_records.inspection_sub: Requested before the work is covered up.
site_records.outstanding_hint: The list attached to the certificate. Practical completion is issued with work outstanding — that is normal.
site_records.certify_sub: This releases retention and starts the defects clock.
site_records.certify_note: Practical completion is refused while a critical defect or an open non-conformance is on the register — certifying over one signs away the leverage to have it fixed.
site_records.completion_blocked: There are {count} open critical defects or non-conformances. Practical completion cannot be certified over them.
site_records.already_a_variation: That instruction already has a change request against it.

meetings.title: Meetings
meetings.subtitle: Agenda, minutes, who was in the room, and what has to be done about it.
meetings.project_hint: Actions can only become tasks on a project, so a meeting without one keeps its actions in the minutes.
meetings.minutes_outstanding_title: {count} meeting(s) held with no minutes circulated
meetings.minutes_outstanding_body: This is where decisions quietly evaporate.
meetings.agenda_hint: Sent before the meeting; it becomes the structure of the minutes.
meetings.minutes_note: Attendance is recorded with the minutes on purpose: “it was agreed at the site meeting” is only an argument if the record says who was there to agree it.
meetings.actions_note: Actions become tasks on the project — an action that lives only in minutes is one nobody works.
meetings.confirm_remove_body: “{title}” and its minutes are removed. Actions already created stay as tasks.

agile.title: Sprints and backlog
agile.subtitle: Stories are ordinary tasks, so the board, the schedule and the timesheets all still work.
agile.backlog_sub: Unranked items sit at the bottom — an item nobody has prioritised is not the most important one.
agile.epics_sub: Work that spans sprints. Progress is its stories, not a separate estimate that could disagree with them.
agile.releases_sub: What went out, and what was in it.
agile.no_active_hint: Plan one, put stories in it, then start it.
agile.no_goal: No goal set — a sprint without one is just a timebox.
agile.goal_hint: One sentence. If you cannot write it, the sprint has no goal.
agile.revision_hint: Without it, “what was in this version” is a guess six months from now.
agile.close_note: Unfinished stories go back to the backlog, not forward into the next sprint — carrying them automatically is how the next sprint starts full before anybody plans it.
agile.one_at_a_time: Another sprint is already running on this project. Two at once makes velocity and the burn-down ambiguous.
agile.not_active: Only a running sprint can be closed.

portal.title: Your projects
portal.subtitle: What is happening on your jobs, and what needs you.
portal.empty_body: The portal shows projects you are attached to as a client or a contractor. If you work here, your projects are under Projects.
portal.progress_note: This is the same figure the delivery team sees — it is not calculated separately for you.
portal.changes_sub: Variations to scope, cost or dates
portal.no_work: Nothing assigned to you right now.
portal.time_sub: Goes through the same approval as everybody else's timesheet.
portal.claims_sub: What has been certified, and what is still with them
portal.documents_sub: Everything on this job you can see, and anywhere to send us something
portal.rate_sub: One rating a month — it goes straight to the delivery team.
portal.rate_dialog_sub: Honest is more useful than kind. Nobody is scored on this individually.
portal.not_rated: You have not rated this month yet.
portal.my_invoices_sub: Prepare an invoice for your work and send it to the project manager.
portal.new_invoice_sub: Your reference and the period this covers.
portal.no_invoices: You have not invoiced on this project yet.
portal.invoice_reference_hint: As it appears on your own invoice.
portal.cinvoice_empty: Add at least one line, or attach your invoice, before sending it.
portal.cinvoice_sent: This invoice has already been sent and can no longer be changed.
portal.my_contracts_sub: What you are working under on this job.
portal.task_raised: Your request has been sent to the project team.
portal.raise_request_sub: It goes straight to the people running this project.
portal.your_requests_sub: What you have asked for, and where it got to
portal.no_requests: You have not asked for anything yet.
portal.delivery_sub: Delivered, outstanding and late, per project.

assistant.title: Assistant
assistant.subtitle: What the data says needs your attention, and a hand with the writing.
assistant.all_clear_hint: Every active project is reporting, inside its indices, and has no stalled decisions.
assistant.draft_sub: The figures are taken from the project; the model only writes the words around them.
assistant.draft_warning: A draft. Read it before you send it — the numbers are real, the sentences are not yours yet.
assistant.no_provider: No AI provider is configured on this workspace, so drafting is unavailable. Everything above is calculated from your data and does not need one.
assistant.slipping_detail: {name} has earned {spi} of the value it planned to by now.
assistant.overspend_detail: {name} is returning {cpi} of value for what it has spent.
assistant.overloaded_detail: {hours} hours planned against a {capacity}-hour month, across {projects} projects.
assistant.silent_title: {count} active project(s) have reported nothing for two weeks
assistant.silent_detail: A project reporting nothing is not a project going well — it is one nobody can say anything about.
assistant.risk_title: {count} high risk(s) with no mitigation written
assistant.risk_detail: Scored 15 or more, and nothing recorded about what is being done.
assistant.change_title: {count} change request(s) waiting more than a week
assistant.change_detail: Submitted and still undecided. The plan and the decision are drifting apart.

alerts.deadline_title: {count} task(s) due in the next {days} days
alerts.overdue_detail: They are still open, and the dates on the plan no longer mean anything.
alerts.budget_title: {pct}% of the budget is accounted for

chat.title: Project chat
chat.subtitle: For the conversation that has no task yet.

equipment.title: Equipment checks
equipment.sub: Pre-use inspections — the value is the unbroken run, not any one of them
equipment.identifier_hint: Scan it or type it. A code that matches nothing on file is still worth recording.
equipment.signed_hint: Your name, the time and your address are recorded — the same as signing a document.

contractors.title: Subcontractor invoices
contractors.subtitle: What contractors have sent in for work on your projects.
contractors.markup_hint: Optional, and never shown to the client or the contractor. Leave blank for none.
contractors.reject_sub: The contractor is shown your reason, so write something they can act on.
contractors.no_contractors: No contractors on this project yet.
contractors.no_email: This contractor has no email address, so the contract cannot be sent.
contractors.not_submitted: Only a submitted invoice can be approved or rejected.
contractors.register_sub: Everyone you subcontract to, and everything about them.
contractors.register_empty: No subcontractors yet. Add the first one.
contractors.add_sub: Their name and how to reach them. Give them a project and they get portal access to invoice you.
contractors.from_suppliers: These are your supplier records. Adding one here adds it to Supplier Management too.
contractors.field_project_hint: Optional. They are invited to the portal once they are on a job.
contractors.engage_sub: They are invited to the portal if they have not been already.
contractors.no_work: Nothing assigned to them on this project.
contractors.their_invoices_sub: Everything they have sent in, across every project.
contractors.our_signatory_hint: They are told in the app, and the contract waits for their signature here.

contracts.title: Contracts
contracts.subtitle: Project contracts — drafted, amended, reviewed and signed here.
contracts.draft_sub: Start from one of your templates, or from nothing at all.
contracts.template_hint: Your own project templates. Leave blank to write the terms yourself.
contracts.title_hint: Leave blank to name it after the contractor and the project.
contracts.no_body: This contract has no wording yet.
contracts.no_body_hint: Amend it to write the terms, or draft the next one from a template.
contracts.amend_sub: Strike the clauses that do not apply, or change the terms. This writes a new version.
contracts.amend_withdraws: This contract is out for signature. Amending it withdraws the signatures already requested, and the parties will be asked to sign the new version.
contracts.change_note_hint: Recorded against this version — "removed clause 7, no plant on this package".
contracts.submit_explainer: This goes to whoever your company has set to approve contracts. If no approval steps are set up, it is marked approved and ready to sign.
contracts.signature_stale: Signed against an earlier version. The wording has changed since.
contracts.your_signature_needed: This contract is waiting for your signature
contracts.signing_as_contractor: You are signing as the contractor.
contracts.signing_as_company: You are countersigning for the company.
contracts.type_your_name_hint: Typing your name here is your signature.
contracts.decline_reason_hint: The other party is shown this, and has to be able to act on it.
contracts.send_explainer: {contractor} signs first, then the person you choose below countersigns.
contracts.closed: A signed or cancelled contract can no longer be changed.
contracts.not_submittable: Only a draft or a rejected contract can be submitted for review.
contracts.not_in_review: This contract is not in review.
contracts.not_sendable: Only an approved or draft contract can be sent for signature.
contracts.no_body_to_sign: This contract has no wording to sign.
contracts.no_counterparty: This contract has no contractor, so it cannot be sent.
contracts.already_decided: This signature has already been given or refused.
contracts.decline_reason_required: A refusal has to say why.
contracts.not_your_turn: The earlier party has not signed yet.
contracts.not_yours_to_sign: This contract is not waiting on your signature.
contracts.no_signatory_email: The chosen signatory has no email address, so the contract cannot be sent.
contracts.mail_signature_line: You have been nominated to sign contract {number} with {contractor} on {project}.
contracts.inapp_signature: Contract {number} with {contractor} is waiting for your signature.
contracts.member_hint: Who the contract is with. Needed before it can be sent for signature.
contracts.no_contractors_on_project: No contractors on this project yet — add one on the Subcontractors screen first.
contracts.waiting_on_other_party: It is now with the other party for their signature.
contracts.name_alongside_drawing: Your name in text as well, so the record stays legible.
contracts.reopen_reason_hint: Every party who signed is told this.
contracts.reopen_warning: This contract is signed. Reopening tells everybody who signed, returns it to draft, and it must be signed again.
contracts.not_reopenable: Only a signed contract can be reopened.
contracts.reopen_reason_required: Say why the contract is being reopened.
contracts.not_yours_to_amend: This contract is not yours to change.
contracts.bad_signature_image: That signature could not be read.
contracts.signature_too_large: That signature image is too large.
contracts.mail_reopened_line: Contract {number} on {project} has been reopened for amendment.
contracts.mail_reopened_resign: The wording will change, so it will come back to you to sign again.
contracts.inapp_reopened: Contract {number} has been reopened for amendment.
contracts.need_drawing: Draw your signature above, or switch to Type.
contracts.no_document: No document has been generated for this contract yet.
contracts.bad_signed_pdf: That signed document could not be read as a PDF.
contracts.amendment_would_drop_tables: This change would delete {n} table(s) from the contract — the editor cannot keep them. Edit the wording elsewhere, or ask for the table to be changed in the template.
contracts.sign_steps: Pick or draw a signature, click where it goes on the page, then sign.
contracts.need_a_signature: Pick a saved signature, or draw one.
contracts.place_it_on_the_page: Click the page where your signature should go.
contracts.document_load_failed: The contract document could not be opened.
contracts.signing_failed: The contract could not be signed. Please try again.
contracts.counterparty_has_no_login: This contractor has no login yet, so they could never sign. Invite them to the portal first.
contracts.signatory_cannot_sign: This party has no login, so they cannot sign. Invite them to the portal, then send the contract again.

contract_templates.title: Contract templates
contract_templates.subtitle: The wording this company subcontracts on. Kept here, in Project Management.
contract_templates.kept_here: Templates are kept in Project Management.
contract_templates.form_sub: Write the standard terms once, then amend them per contractor when you draft.
contract_templates.none_hint: Write one, or install the starter set with pm:contract-templates:install.
contract_templates.import_sub: Copy a template out of Contract Management.
contract_templates.import_is_a_copy: Importing takes a copy. Editing it here never changes the original, and it stays yours if Contract Management is removed.
contract_templates.placeholders_hint: These are filled in when a contract is drafted:

steps.title: Board columns
steps.subtitle: Name the steps your work actually moves through. Each one carries a meaning the rest of the module reads — progress, completions and claims all follow the meaning, not the name.
steps.needs_done: One step has to count as Done, or nothing on this board can ever be completed.
steps.will_move: {count} task(s) sit in a step you removed. They will move to the first column.
steps.unknown_step: “{step}” is not a column on this project.
steps.at_least_one: A board needs at least one column.
steps.too_many: A board is limited to {max} columns; beyond that nobody can read it.
steps.bad_category: “{label}” has to count as one of the built-in states.

billing.no_accounting: Accounting is not installed, so nothing can be billed to the ledger.
billing.no_party: No accounting customer matches "{client}" — create one, or merge the duplicates.

monitoring.title: Monitoring
monitoring.subtitle: Changes, findings and matches awaiting a decision

data_sources.title: Data sources
data_sources.subtitle: Which sources this company verifies suppliers against, what each one may answer, and which checks nobody can answer yet.
data_sources.ledger_broken: The evidence chain does not reconcile at entry {at} ({reason}). Treat the affected evidence as unverified until it has been investigated.
data_sources.coverage_help: Every check the module knows how to make, and who answers it today. A check with no source is not skipped — it is recorded as unavailable until somebody performs it and records what they found.
data_sources.manual_notice: {count} check(s) have no configured source, so a person has to perform them and record what they found.
data_sources.enable_help: While this is off, the checks it would answer are recorded as unavailable rather than passing.
data_sources.credentials_help: Encrypted at rest and never sent back to this screen. Add a key to replace it; keys you do not retype are kept.
data_sources.default_for_help: Where more than one source can answer a check, this one is asked first.
data_sources.monthly_quota_help: Metered sources cost money per call. Once the allowance is spent, checks record as unavailable instead of billing you.
data_sources.endpoints_help: The address your authorised account provides for each check. Placeholders are filled from the supplier.
data_sources.endpoint_hint: Placeholders: registration_number, company_name, vat_number, tax_reference_number, account_number, reference
data_sources.manual_provider_note: Always available. A person performs the check at the source and records what they found — it lands in the same observation log, with the same evidence entry, attributed to them.
data_sources.profiled: {count} check(s) already know where to call. Enter your credentials and they will work — the fields below are only for a contract that differs.

verifications.title: Due diligence
verifications.payment_held: Payment is held on this supplier
verifications.outstanding: {count} check(s) still need attention before this supplier should be treated as verified.
verifications.record_help: For a check you performed at the source yourself. It is stored with the same evidence trail as an automated one, attributed to you — so nobody later mistakes it for a machine-verified answer.
verifications.observed_help: Type what the source actually displayed. It is compared against what the supplier told us, field by field, so a difference is caught rather than taken on trust.
verifications.pin_held: A PIN is held for this supplier, so their tax compliance status can be verified.
verifications.pin_missing: No PIN yet. The supplier's TCS PIN is their authorisation for you to verify their tax compliance status.
verifications.pin_help: Stored encrypted, and used only to verify tax compliance status. A verification records what SARS said at the moment it was asked — which is why this is not a certificate upload.

errors.no_source: No source is configured for {check}, so it cannot be run automatically. Record the check yourself, or configure a source under Configure → Data sources.

ownership.title: Ownership
ownership.no_ubos: No natural person has been resolved yet. Until the chain reaches people, there is nobody to screen — a company cannot be sanctioned and cannot be a PEP.
ownership.diagram_alt: Ownership diagram. The same information is in the table below it.
ownership.table_caption: Every ownership stake on record. This table is the full picture — the diagram above shows the same relationships.
ownership.as_at_help: The date this holding was true. An ownership record with no date is a claim about no particular time.
ownership.unallocated: {entity}: {missing}% of the shareholding is unaccounted for. Somebody holds it and has not been named.
ownership.unstated_stakes: {entity}: {n} stake(s) recorded without a size, so the shareholding cannot be resolved.
ownership.over_allocated: {entity}: declared stakes come to {declared}%, which is more than the whole company.
ownership.related_help: Suppliers sharing a person or a holding company with this one. Frequently innocent — and also how one group bids a tender under three names.
ownership.existing_company: A company already in the chain
ownership.owns_what_help: The supplier itself, or a company higher up the chain.
ownership.compare_help: Enter the beneficial owners exactly as the registry lists them. They are compared against the people this supplier's chain resolves to — the gap between the two lists is the finding.

risk.title: Risk assessment
risk.never_assessed: This supplier has not been assessed yet. Until it is, nothing here says whether they are safe to trade with.
risk.trend_alt: Risk score trend over the last {n} assessments.
risk.gates_pass: Every approval gate passes. This supplier can be approved without further review.
risk.tier_unset: Not set — the engagement decides how much diligence is needed.
risk.tier_help: Answer for this engagement, not for the company in general. The same supplier can be tier 1 for stationery and tier 4 for a payroll integration.
risk.record_hit_help: For a match you found on a published list. It counts against the supplier and monitors exactly like a fetched one.
risk.no_hits: Nothing has come back from screening.
risk.subject: Screened
risk.reason_help: Required when clearing a match. A year from now, an unexplained dismissal cannot be told apart from a mis-click.

reputation.title: Reputation & social monitoring
reputation.no_source_notice: No news or social source is configured, so nothing can be searched automatically. A supplier nobody could search must not be mistaken for one nothing was found about.
reputation.no_coverage: Nothing has been searched for this supplier yet. That is not a clean record — it is an absence of one.
reputation.needs_review_notice: {n} mention(s) could not be tied to this supplier with confidence. They are not counted until somebody confirms they are the right company.
reputation.attributed: {n}% confident this is about this supplier
reputation.attribution_warning: We are only {n}% confident this mention is about this supplier. Confirm it is the right company before treating it as a finding.
reputation.reason_help: Required when clearing a finding. A year from now, an unexplained dismissal cannot be told apart from a mis-click.
reputation.watching_help: A supplier is rarely named by the company on its invoice. Brands, trading names, websites and platform handles are all searched, along with current directors and beneficial owners.
reputation.nothing_watched: Only the registered name, trading name and current people.
reputation.watch_help: Add a brand, a website or a platform account. Handles are per platform, because the same name on two platforms is two different accounts.

passport.health_help: How this relationship is going — delivery, paperwork, responsiveness.
passport.health_unknown: Too early to say. Nothing has been asked of them and nothing delivered yet.
passport.questionnaires_missing: Not yet sent for this tier: {packs}.
passport.blacklisted: This party is on the blacklist
passport.never_assessed: Never assessed. Nothing here says whether this supplier is safe to trade with.
passport.not_searched: Not searched. That is an absence of a record, not a clean one.
passport.can_be_run: A source is configured — this can be run
passport.needs_a_person: No source configured; somebody must check it
passport.no_case: No case has been opened for this supplier.
passport.conditions_lapsed: The conditions were due {date} and have not been met. This approval should not be relied on.
passport.edd_because: Enhanced due diligence is required because
passport.no_ubos: No natural person has been resolved. Until the chain reaches people, there is nobody to screen.
passport.moves_to: Moves the case to {state}. This is a {slot} decision.
passport.conditions_due_help: An approval subject to conditions with no deadline is an approval.
passport.override_help: An override is recorded on the case with what was failing at the time.

monitoring.title: Monitoring inbox
monitoring.subtitle: Everything across every supplier that nobody has looked at yet — changes on the sources, findings in the press, and screening matches.
monitoring.due_help: Suppliers whose checks have gone stale. This is work nobody has been alerted to yet — an unanswered question does not become less urgent by being ignored.
monitoring.note_help: Required when dismissing. A year from now, an unexplained dismissal cannot be told apart from a mis-click.
monitoring.no_sources: No source is configured for any of the due checks, so nothing was re-run. The gaps are recorded rather than hidden.
monitoring.runs_no_source: {n} monitoring pass(es) found no configured source for at least one check.
monitoring.cases_help: Due-diligence cases waiting on somebody. Overdue first.

appraisals.title: Supplier performance
appraisals.subtitle: What has been appraised, and how it is trending
appraisals.templates_subtitle: The questions a supplier is scored against, and the weight each one carries
appraisals.no_templates: No scorecards yet. Create one before appraising a supplier.
appraisals.industry_optional_hint: Leave empty to use this scorecard for any industry
appraisals.cannot_delete: In use by an appraisal — retire it instead
appraisals.delete_confirm: Delete "{name}" and its questions? This cannot be undone.
appraisals.weight_ok: The weights total 100%. This scorecard can award full marks.
appraisals.weight_over_hint: The weights total more than 100%, so a supplier could score above full marks.
appraisals.weight_under_hint: The weights total less than 100%, so no supplier can score more than this. {short}% is unassigned.
appraisals.question: Question
appraisals.minimum_hint: Below this, the question is marked failed (1–5)
appraisals.no_questions: No questions yet. A scorecard with none cannot appraise anything.
appraisals.no_answers: No answers were recorded for this appraisal.
appraisals.trend_help: Months with no appraisals are left out rather than shown as zero.

offboarding.title: Offboarding
offboarding.subtitle: Manage employee exit processes, checklists and exit interviews
offboarding.no_plans_sub: Start by creating an offboarding plan for a departing employee.
offboarding.analytics_subtitle: Turnover insight across every offboarding plan
offboarding.reports_filter_hint: Filters apply to every report. The status filter applies only to reports that support it.
offboarding.reports_plan_summary_desc: Every offboarding plan with employee detail, termination type, completion %, rehire eligibility and counter-offer outcomes.
offboarding.reports_exit_interviews_desc: Every completed exit interview — reason for leaving, satisfaction scores, would-recommend answers and qualitative feedback.

packs.title: Regulatory Packs
packs.subtitle: The rulebooks that classify incidents and set statutory deadlines
packs.empty: No regulatory pack has been installed on this system yet. Until one is installed and activated, incidents cannot be reported — ask your system administrator to run the SHEQ regulatory pack installation.
packs.no_sites_hint: No active sites are set up yet, so this can only be activated company-wide.
packs.site_type_mismatch: This pack is written for {types}. {sites} are not of those types — activate it anyway only if you are sure.
packs.preview_hint: A preview is a sandbox: it does not seed the legal register and does not create real statutory obligations.
packs.supersede_hint: Activating supersedes whatever is in force for the same scope. The previous activation is kept on record, because which rulebook applied and when is itself evidence.

legal.title: Legal Register
legal.subtitle: Statutory requirements seeded from the active regulatory packs
legal.needs_company: Choose a company to see its legal register.
legal.no_evidence: Nothing linked yet, so this requirement cannot be assessed.
legal.act_hint: Link the document that proves it, then record when it was met; the next review follows from the clause's frequency.

incident.report_subtitle: Four fields is enough — detail can follow
incident.what_happened_hint: Describe it plainly, as you would tell a colleague
incident.no_sites: No sites configured yet — leave blank
incident.potential_hint: What could this have caused, at worst?
incident.potential_hint_high: High potential — this will require a full investigation
incident.incapacity_hint: 14 or more may make this reportable
incident.machinery_failure: Machinery failed or ran out of control
incident.anonymous_hint: Your identity will not be stored on this record
incident.classification_note: On submission this is classified against your active regulatory pack, and any statutory deadlines start immediately.
incident.context_explainer: Captured when the incident was reported and frozen — this is what was true at the time.
incident.no_gaps_detail: Nothing was flagged against the people, equipment or location involved.
incident.affected_external: Or a name not on the staff list
incident.affected_external_hint: A visitor, driver or contractor employee

obligation.title: Statutory Obligations
obligation.subtitle: What the regulator requires, and by when

no_company.title: No active company
no_company.body: SHEQ records belong to a company. You are signed in as a platform administrator, which sits above any single tenant — choose the company you want to work in.
no_company.body_self_hosted: No company has been set up on this installation yet. SHEQ records belong to a company, so create one under Settings before using the module.

hazard.report_subtitle: Something unsafe you have noticed — one line is enough
hazard.what_is_wrong_hint: e.g. Handrail missing on the gantry stairs
hazard.how_bad_hint: Your best guess — a practitioner will confirm
hazard.you_will_hear_back: You will be told what happens to this report, including if it is not taken forward.
hazard.list_subtitle: Reported hazards and their triage state
hazard.reason_hint: The reporter is told this. A rejection without a reason stops people reporting.
hazard.link_hint: Use this when the hazard turned out to be the incident. Otherwise the two stay separate records of one event, and the incident carries no sign that somebody had flagged the risk beforehand.

action.title: Actions
action.subtitle: One list, whatever raised it
action.extend_reason_hint: Recorded against the action and counted — extensions are visible, not silent.
action.hierarchy_hint: Prefer elimination or engineering over telling people to be careful

risk.title: Risk Assessments
risk.subtitle: Assessed hazards, their controls and when each is due for review
risk.empty: No risk assessments yet. One is required before construction work starts.
risk.add_note: Created as a draft. Add hazard lines and controls, then send it for approval — an unapproved assessment is not a control.

permits.title: Permits to Work
permits.subtitle: High-risk work that may not start without written authority
permits.add_note: A requested permit is not a valid one. It authorises nothing until it has been issued after its pre-issue checks pass.

inspections.title: Inspections
inspections.subtitle: The schedule that must not slip, and what has been completed
inspections.schedules_hint: An overdue schedule is a control that has stopped running
inspections.empty_schedules: No inspection schedules. Nothing is being checked on a cycle.

competency.title: Competency
competency.subtitle: Who is qualified and appointed to do what, and when that lapses
competency.records_hint: Sorted by expiry — this register answers who is about to lapse
competency.add_note: Defines what the competency is. Records for individual people are captured against it, and expire on the validity you set here.
competency.record_note: A qualification earned elsewhere — a first-aid certificate, a rigging ticket, a licence. Leave the expiry blank and the competency's own validity period sets it.
competency.expiry_hint: Blank means the competency's validity period decides.
competency.evidence_hint: The certificate itself. Stored with the record and downloadable from it.

documents.title: Documents
documents.subtitle: Controlled procedures: what is published, and what is overdue for review
documents.add_note: Created as a draft with version 1. A draft is invisible to readers until you publish it — nobody can follow a procedure they cannot see.
documents.publish_note: This version becomes the one in force. The previous one is superseded, and anybody who acknowledged the superseded text has to confirm the new one.
documents.awaiting_publish: {count} procedure(s) written and not yet in force
documents.awaiting_publish_hint: A draft is a procedure nobody is following: it does not appear in the document library and nobody can be asked to acknowledge it.

contractors.title: Contractors
contractors.subtitle: Who may be on site, and what is stopping the rest
contractors.hint: Blocked first — those are people who must not be on site
contractors.empty_expiring: Nothing expiring in the next 30 days.
contractors.add_note: A new contractor is blocked from site until every mandatory document is present and in date. That is the default on purpose.
contractors.from_supplier_hint: Choosing a supplier fills the rest of this form from their record and ties the safety file to the commercial one. Leave it empty for a contractor who is not a supplier.
contractors.from_supplier_filled: Filled from the supplier record. Anything you had already typed was left as you typed it.

sites.title: Sites
sites.subtitle: Where work happens — every SHEQ record hangs off one of these
sites.mirrored: Sites mirror your Company Structure. Add a unit there and it appears here overnight.
sites.empty: No sites yet. Run the structure sync, or add units in Company Settings.

registers.stored_in_db: Stored in the database, compressed and encrypted at rest
registers.attach_hint: Drag files here, several at once, or one zip — a zip becomes one controlled document per file inside it. Stored in the database, compressed and encrypted at rest.

audience.site: Only people at this document’s site
audience.hint: A safety procedure nobody can find protects nobody, so everyone is the default. Restriction is the exception.

analysis.title: BI Analysis
analysis.subtitle: Twelve months of safety performance, from the stored KPI projection
analysis.no_snapshots: No KPI snapshots yet — the projection is built nightly by sheq:kpis:compute.
analysis.gaps: {count} of these months have no snapshot — shown as a gap, never as zero.

reports.title: BI Reports
reports.subtitle: The monthly safety report, assembled from what the module holds
reports.no_narrative: Numbers only. The written commentary needs the AI Safety Officer, which is not built — an invented narrative in a safety report is worse than none.

conflicts.title: Needs Your Attention
conflicts.subtitle: Where a device and the server disagreed. Both values are kept — you decide.
conflicts.all_clear: No conflicts. Every device change has been applied or resolved.
conflicts.rejected_operations: {count} device operations were refused and are on record.
conflicts.confirm_device: The device value will be written to the record.
conflicts.confirm_server: The server value stands. The device value stays on record.
conflicts.both_kept: Both values stay on record whichever you choose.

forms.title: Statutory Forms
forms.subtitle: Forms the regulator requires, pre-filled from the incident record
forms.outstanding: {count} required form(s) have not been produced. Statutory deadlines are running.
forms.none_reportable: No reportable incidents. Nothing is owed to a regulator.
forms.gaps_headline: {count} field(s) the records could not fill
forms.gaps_hint: Nothing has been guessed. Fill each one in, or the form cannot be submitted.
forms.complete_ready: Every required field is filled. This form is ready to be finalised.
forms.final_frozen: Finalised {at}. This is the record of what was submitted and no longer changes.
forms.reason_hint: Kept on the audit record beside the original value
forms.submit_body: Finalising freezes the form as the record of what was submitted. It cannot be edited afterwards.
forms.submitted_body: This is the record of what was submitted. Generate a new form if anything changed.
forms.finalise_blocked: {count} field(s) still to fill before this can be submitted.

settings.title: SHEQ Settings
settings.subtitle: Employer particulars, reference formats and operating rules
settings.employer_hint: These appear on every statutory form. A W.Cl.2 cannot be submitted without the COIDA number.
settings.coida_hint: Required on the W.Cl.2 employer's report of an accident
settings.coida_missing_title: No COIDA registration number on record
settings.coida_missing_body: Add it now and every W.Cl.2 generated afterwards will carry it.
settings.coida_missing_with_incidents: {count} reportable incident(s) are on record and none of their W.Cl.2 forms can be submitted without it.
settings.registered_name_hint: Where it differs from the trading name
settings.references_hint: The prefix on every reference issued. Changing it does not renumber what already exists.
settings.triage_sla_hint: How long a reported hazard may wait before someone assesses it
settings.effectiveness_days_hint: How long after closing an action before its effectiveness is checked
settings.anonymous_hint: A worker who fears blame reports nothing. Turning this off suppresses reporting.
settings.contractor_requirements_hint: Nobody from a contractor comes on site until every one of these is on file and in date. Ticking a box here blocks contractors who were working yesterday.
settings.contractor_requirements_site_note: This is the company default. A site can demand its own list instead — set that on the site itself, under Sites.
settings.contractor_requirements_none: Nothing is demanded, so a contractor is compliant the moment they are registered. That is a decision you may make; it is not the shipped default.

inspections.templates_subtitle: The checklists your inspections run from
inspections.no_templates: No templates yet. An inspection has nothing to ask without one.
inspections.question: Question
inspections.critical_hint: A critical question that fails fails the whole inspection, whatever the score. A missing fire extinguisher is not offset by tidy housekeeping.
inspections.code_hint: Capitals, numbers and hyphens — e.g. CON-SCAFFOLD
inspections.need_template_first: You need a published template before anything can be scheduled.
inspections.signed_hint: The name of the person who carried out this inspection
inspections.install_library: The standard library of 20 checklists across ten industries installs automatically. If it is still empty, ask your system administrator to run the SHEQ library install.

investigations.title: Investigations
investigations.subtitle: What happened, why it happened, and what stops it happening again
investigations.heading: Investigation
investigations.none_open: Nothing under investigation. Incidents appear here when they are reported.
investigations.only_blames_people: Every root cause so far blames a person or team. Look for the task, environmental or organisational condition that allowed it — otherwise the fix is discipline, not prevention.
investigations.layer_hint_organisational: The decision, procedure or resourcing that set it up
investigations.layer_hint_task_environment: The conditions people were working in
investigations.layer_hint_individual_team_action: What somebody did or did not do
investigations.layer_hint_absent_failed_defence: The barrier that should have stopped it
investigations.evidence_hint: A statement, a photograph, a record — what a reader could check
investigations.summary_hint: What a reader who was not there needs to understand
investigations.depth_hint: Depth follows potential severity, not what actually happened — a near miss that could have killed is investigated like a fatality.
investigations.confirm_body_submit: The investigation can no longer be edited once submitted. Reopen the incident if it needs revisiting.
investigations.confirm_body_approve: Approving accepts the root cause as the organisation's finding. The incident can then be closed once its actions and obligations are discharged.
investigations.confirm_body_close: Closing records that the organisation has dealt with this. It can be reopened later, with a reason.
investigations.confirm_body_reopen: A new revision is created. The current one is preserved exactly as it stands and stays readable.
investigations.reopen_hint: Kept on the record beside the revision it created

ai.title: AI Safety Officer
ai.subtitle: Drafts prepared by the assistant, waiting for a person to decide.
ai.boundary_body: The assistant proposes; it never records. Nothing on this page has any effect until you accept it, and your name goes on what you accept.
ai.unverified_waiting: {count} draft(s) make claims with no supporting source. Those are listed first.
ai.queue_empty: Nothing waiting. Drafts appear here when the assistant is asked for one.
ai.no_source: No supporting source — check this before accepting
ai.note_hint: Required to reject. It is the clearest signal about where the assistant is going wrong.
ai.reviewed_n: {n} of {total} drafts reviewed by a person
ai.never_body: These decisions carry personal legal liability. They are reserved to a named person and the assistant is blocked from them in code, not merely instructed to avoid them.
ai.chat_scope: Answers come from this company’s SHEQ records and reference material. Nothing here changes a record.
ai.chat_empty: Ask a question about safety at this employer.
ai.chat_placeholder: What do you need to know?
ai.chat_failed: The assistant could not be reached. Nothing was recorded.

approvals.subtitle: Decisions waiting on you, and requests you raised.
approvals.designer_subtitle: Design who approves what, per company.
approvals.no_approver: No one can fill this step
approvals.versioned: Requests already in progress keep the steps they started under.
approvals.no_users: No users found for this company.

audits.subtitle: Internal, supplier and certification audits.
audits.clause_required: A non-conformance must cite the clause it breaches.
audits.root_cause_hint: Why it happened — not what you did about it.
audits.correction_hint: What was done, and what stops it happening again.

suppliers.subtitle: SHEQ assessment before a supplier works on site.
suppliers.invite_note: The invitation names the documents this risk band has to produce, so they are sent once rather than discovered one rejection at a time.

ppe.title: PPE
ppe.subtitle: What was issued, to whom, and when it is due for replacement.
ppe.lifespan_hint: Used to compute the replacement date automatically
ppe.on_hand_hint: The count after checking the shelf
ppe.empty_catalogue: Nothing in the catalogue yet, so there is nothing to issue. Use “Manage catalogue and stock” to add the items this company issues — boots, helmets, gloves — and set how many are on the shelf.
ppe.issue_note: What was handed over, to whom. The replacement date follows from the item's lifespan.
ppe.size_hint: This item is issued in sizes.
ppe.serial_hint: For items that are tested or recalled individually, such as a harness.

medical.title: Medical surveillance
medical.subtitle: Fitness for work, and examinations falling due.
medical.clinical_hint: Health information. Encrypted, and visible only with the clinical-data permission.
medical.clinical_failed: The clinical detail could not be loaded. Nothing is shown rather than an empty record, which would read as no findings.
medical.clinical_warning: Health information under POPIA s26. Reading it is recorded against your account.
medical.record_note: An examination that has been done. The clinical detail is kept separately and only read by those entitled to.
medical.expires_hint: Leave empty to use the validity period set for this examination.
medical.restrictions_hint: Required. A restriction nobody wrote down leaves a supervisor guessing.
medical.clinical_encrypted: Encrypted at rest and read only by those entitled to clinical detail.

environmental.title: Environmental
environmental.subtitle: Water, energy, fuel, waste and carbon.
environmental.no_factor: These meters have no emission factor, so they add nothing to the carbon total:
environmental.record_note: A meter reading, dated. The carbon total is recalculated from it using the meter's emission factor.

equipment.title: Safety equipment
equipment.subtitle: Extinguishers, harnesses, lifting gear and first aid.

visitors.title: Visitors
visitors.subtitle: Approval, induction, and who is on site right now.
visitors.roll_call: This is the roll call. After an alarm, it is the only list that matters.
visitors.no_workflow_detail: No approval workflow is configured for visitors, so there is nobody authorised to admit anyone. Set one up first — this is refused rather than allowed through, because an unconfigured approval means nobody has decided who may sign, not that anyone may.
visitors.request_note: A visit has to be approved before anybody is admitted, so this is a request rather than an arrival.
visitors.expected_to_hint: After this time the visitor is listed as overstaying.

emergency.title: Emergency
emergency.subtitle: Plans, assembly points and drill performance.
emergency.uncovered: No emergency plan has been written for: {types}. Nobody has a procedure to follow for these.
emergency.record_drill_note: A drill that was held. The number unaccounted for is what decides whether it passed.
emergency.unaccounted_hint: The number that decides pass or fail.
emergency.improvements_hint: Each one becomes an action somebody owns.

training.title: Safety training
training.subtitle: Read from Learning Management. Records are not duplicated here.
training.unavailable: Learning Management is not installed, so there is no training data to show.

integrations.title: Gate integrations
integrations.subtitle: Connect your access control or clock-in system. Enter the credentials, test, then enforce.
integrations.none: No connections yet. Add one to start checking people at the gate.
integrations.label: Name
integrations.impact_body: {refused} of {total} recent entries would have been refused.
integrations.monitor_first: New connections start in monitor mode: refusals are recorded but nobody is stopped. Watch it for a week, clear the backlog, then enforce.
integrations.enforce_warning: From now on, people who fail a check will be stopped at the gate. Based on the last 30 days, {refused} entries would have been refused. Make sure that backlog is cleared first.

inductions.subtitle: What people are told before they set foot on site.
inductions.author: Author an induction
inductions.requires_nda: Require an agreement to be accepted
inductions.bulk_how: Download the template, fill it in, upload it. Check it first — nothing is saved until you press Import.

talks.not_reached: {count} people have not been reached this month
talks.record_note: A talk with no attendance proves something was prepared, not that anybody was told.

ppe_config.search: Search by code, name or barcode
ppe_config.read_only: You can view this configuration but not change it.
ppe_config.empty_help: Nothing in the catalogue yet. Add the items this company issues — boots, helmets, gloves — then set how many are on the shelf. The issue register reads from here.
ppe_config.low_warning: {n} stock line(s) at or below the reorder level.
ppe_config.life_hint: Used to work out the replacement date automatically
ppe_config.sized_hint: Tick this when the item is issued in sizes, so stock is counted per size.
ppe_config.on_hand_hint: The count after checking the shelf
ppe_config.reorder_hint: Warn when the count falls to this
ppe_config.size_na: This item is not issued in sizes
ppe_config.site_hint: Leave empty when the stock is not held per site
ppe_config.no_items: No items in the catalogue yet.
ppe_config.stock_hint: One line per item, size and site. Sized PPE is counted per size, because running out of one size is not running out of the item.

import.title: Import PPE items
import.subtitle: Load a catalogue from a spreadsheet instead of typing it.
import.matched_on_code: Items are matched on code — an existing code is updated, not duplicated.

sites.requirements_hint: A refinery and an office park should not demand the same paperwork. Set this site's own list, or leave it following the company.
sites.requirements_inherit_hint: Following means this site changes whenever the company list changes. Turning it off freezes nothing — the site simply states its own.
sites.requirements_none_warning: With nothing ticked, any contractor at this site is compliant the moment they are registered.

flash.requirements_saved: What this site demands has been saved.

triage.title: Triage queue
triage.subtitle: Incidents waiting for somebody to pick them up, latest deadline first.
triage.dialog_help: Confirm how bad this could have been and name who will see it through. Changing the rating moves the deadline.
triage.potential_hint: What could have happened, not what did. 5 could have killed somebody.

alert.title: Safety alerts
alert.subtitle: Carrying a finding to the people exposed to the same hazard.
alert.awaiting_subtitle: Investigations approved with no alert issued.
alert.why_hint: The root cause, not the description again.
alert.needs_why: Say why it happened or what was changed before issuing this.

injury.title: Injury cases
injury.subtitle: Who is off work, who is on light duty, and who is back.
injury.untracked_subtitle: Somebody was hurt and no case was opened.
injury.timeline_help: The day counts are worked out from these periods.
injury.still_running: This person has an open period with no end date, so the day count is still running.
injury.event_hint: Booked off and restricted duty count days. The others are the record of care.
injury.to_hint: Leave blank while it is ongoing.

permit.blocked_title: This permit cannot be issued yet
permit.clear_to_issue: Nothing is blocking this permit. It may be issued.
permit.no_workers: No workers are named on this permit.
permit.no_approvals: No approval steps are configured for this permit type.
permit.suspend_hint: The crew sees this reason, so say what must be fixed before work resumes.
permit.override_warning: You are accepting, against your name, that somebody may do work they are not currently ticketed for. This is recorded on the permit and in the audit trail.
permit.no_closure_checks: This permit type declares no closure checks.

board.title: Live Permit Board
board.subtitle: The work under written authority right now
board.uncovered: {count} live permit(s) have no approved risk assessment covering the site. The authority the permit rests on does not exist.
board.empty: No permits are live. Nothing is being worked under written authority right now.

ra.needs_lines: Add at least one hazard line before this can be approved.
ra.needs_participants: Record who took part before this can be approved — the Construction Regulations and the MHSA both require it.
ra.weak_control_line: Line {sequence}: {hazard} is a high or critical risk controlled only by administrative measures or PPE.
ra.approved_locked: An approved assessment cannot be edited. Create a revision instead; this version stays on the record because incidents were judged against it.
ra.no_lines: No hazard lines yet. An assessment with no lines blocks every permit that references it.
ra.participants_hint: The people doing the work must take part in assessing its risk.
ra.controls_hint: Strongest first. A high risk held only by administrative measures or PPE is flagged.

contractor.subtitle: Whether these people may be on site, and what is stopping them
contractor.blocked_title: These people may not come on site yet
contractor.compliant: This contractor meets what this site demands.
contractor.no_access_events: Nobody has been scanned in or out yet.
contractor.title: Title
contractor.expiry_hint: Leave the expiry blank for a document that does not lapse. A document past its expiry blocks access.
contractor.induction_hint: An induction that has lapsed counts as none, and is the commonest reason a worker is turned away at the gate.
contractor.override_title: Grant access despite an incomplete file
contractor.override_warning: You are accepting, against your name, that these people may be on site without the documents this site requires. Give a date — an override with no end becomes permanent by accident.
contractor.drop_hint: Several at once, or one zip holding the whole safety file — it is unpacked into a document per file.
contractor.photo_hint: How the gatehouse knows the person at the turnstile is the person on the register.
contractor.not_linked: Not linked to a Supplier Management record, so their safety file and their commercial record cannot be read against each other.
contractor.no_assessment: No SHEQ assessment has been done on the commercial side.
contractor.set_aside_note: The document stays on the file as evidence and stops counting towards compliance. Use this to correct a wrong expiry date: attaching the right certificate is not enough on its own, because the check keeps whichever document expires latest.
contractor.set_aside_hint: Recorded against your name. A reviewer asking why a certificate stopped counting reads this.
contractor.pass_hint: A gate scans this and gets a live answer. The code carries nothing but an identifier — no ID number, no medical information, no certificate — so it stays safe to print, photograph and forward.
contractor.worker_site_hint: Leave empty to follow the contractor’s site.
contractor.pass_rotate_warning: The printed card stops working immediately and a new one has to be issued. Use this when a card is lost or somebody has left.
contractor.sites_hint: Approval at one site is never approval at another. A site that blocks this contractor refuses them there whatever their file says elsewhere.
contractor.sites_none: No active sites to decide about yet.
contractor.site_conditions_hint: Printed on the gate verdict when their pass is scanned here. For example: escorted at all times, daylight hours only.
contractor.site_reason_hint: Why this site decided as it did.
contractor.site_reason_required: Required. A block with no reason is a block nobody can lift.
contractor.site_valid_until_hint: Leave empty for an approval that does not lapse.
contractor.site_block_warning: This refuses them at this site only, and it refuses them whatever their company-wide status says.

files.drop_hint: or click to choose. A zip is unpacked into one record per file inside it.

library.title: Document library
library.subtitle: The procedures in force, as they apply to you
library.owing: {count} document(s) are waiting for you to confirm you have read them.
library.empty: No published documents apply to you yet.
library.watermark_note: Every copy carries its version, its publish date and an uncontrolled-copy marking. A printed copy is only current on the day it was printed.

exposure.title: Hours Worked
exposure.subtitle: The exposure every injury rate is divided by
exposure.site_hint: Leave blank for the whole company. Capture per site only if you report per site.
exposure.basis_hint: Where the number came from. Anything but a manual figure makes the month's rates auditable.
exposure.estimated_note: {count} month(s) rest on a manually entered figure, so the rates for them are estimates.
exposure.missing: {count} month(s) have no hours, so LTIFR, TRIR, DIFR and the severity rate cannot be computed for them.
exposure.footnote: Rates are per 200 000 hours worked. A month with no hours is left out of the annual rate rather than counted as zero.

mine.title: Where I Stand
mine.subtitle: My tickets, medicals and reading, as the system has them
mine.no_record: You have no personnel record yet, so there is nothing on file to show. Ask whoever set up your account to add you to the employee list — until then the system cannot tell you where you stand, and it will not guess.
mine.nothing_on_file: Nothing has been recorded against you yet, and nothing has been required of you. This is not the same as being compliant — it means there is nothing to check.
mine.blocking: {count} of your tickets has lapsed and stops you working. You will not be issued a permit or signed onto the task until it is renewed.
mine.awaiting_signature: Waiting for you to sign it
mine.gaps: Required of me and not held
mine.gaps_hint: These have been required of you and there is no record against them. A lapsed ticket is a renewal; these have to be arranged.
mine.induction_not_current: Your site induction is not current. You may be turned away at the gate.
mine.unacknowledged: {count} procedure(s) are waiting for you to confirm you have read them
mine.all_acknowledged: You have confirmed every procedure issued to you.
mine.i_own_review: {document} is due for review and you own it
mine.footnote: This is the same record the registers and the gate read. If something here is wrong, it is wrong everywhere — tell your safety officer rather than working around it.

matrix.title: Competency Matrix
matrix.subtitle: Who is qualified for what, and where we are short
matrix.no_gaps: Every required competency is held by everybody it is required of.
matrix.capped: Showing {shown} of {total} people. The grid is wide by nature, so it is capped.
matrix.nothing_required: No competency has been required of anybody yet. That is not the same as everybody being compliant — it means there is nothing to check against.
matrix.footnote: Requirements attached to a role, department or site are resolved where that context is known; this grid shows the ones attached to people directly. A lapsing ticket still counts as held — it is valid today.

safety_file.title: Safety File
safety_file.subtitle: Every section this host demands, and what is in each.
safety_file.nothing_required: No section is demanded yet, so the file cannot be complete or incomplete. Choose a profile for your industry and adjust it — that is what says which sections matter here.
safety_file.complete: Every demanded section is satisfied. This file does not need a paper copy.
safety_file.history_count: {count} on record. This section is history rather than evidence, so it does not have to be filled.
safety_file.drop_hint: Drop the certificates here. A zip folder is unpacked into one document per file.
safety_file.reason_hint: Recorded against your name, and the contractor is told what it says.
safety_file.valid_until_hint: Leave blank for {months} months from today. It falls out of approval on this date whether or not anybody opens the screen.
safety_file.reject_hint: The contractor has to be told what to fix. A rejection with no reason starts a phone call rather than a corrected document.
safety_file.warning_days_hint: Leave blank to use your default. Set it to the time it actually takes to replace this document.
safety_file.site_hint: Leave blank where it applies at every site. A site-specific document should not block the contractor at the other sites.
safety_file.activities_hint: Leave blank where it applies to all work. A rigging ticket matters for lifting and not for painting.
safety_file.filed_as_hint: Supplied means it has arrived and somebody still has to check it. It satisfies nothing until it is accepted.

state_hint.DRAFT: Nobody has been asked to look at this file yet.
state_hint.SUBMITTED: Handed in and waiting for somebody to pick it up.
state_hint.UNDER_REVIEW: Somebody has it and is going through it.
state_hint.CHANGES_REQUIRED: Sent back. The next submission is a new version.
state_hint.APPROVED: A competent person accepted this file. It stops standing on the date below.
state_hint.SUSPENDED: Not refused, but not standing either. Their people are refused at the gate.
state_hint.EXPIRED: The approval ran out. A fresh file has to be submitted.
state_hint.BLOCKED: Refused. A fresh file has to be submitted.

move_hint.submit: Hands the file to whoever reviews contractor files here. It cannot be submitted while a demanded section is unsatisfied.
move_hint.request_changes: Sends it back with a list of what has to change. The contractor's next submission is a new version, and this one keeps your reason.
move_hint.approve: Accepts the file as it stands today. An approval is a statement about the documents in it on this date, so it carries an expiry.
move_hint.suspend: Stops the approval standing without refusing the file. Their people are refused at the gate until it is reinstated.

safety_file.may_work: Their people may work on site.
safety_file.may_not_work: Their people are refused at the gate.
safety_file.rules_hint: Your decision, not the system's. Every condition below is checked and reported either way; these switches decide which of them actually refuse a contractor at the gate. They apply to every contractor, because applying them unevenly is how a challenge at a boom succeeds.

status_hint.COMPLIANT: Everything demanded is on file, in date and accepted.
status_hint.EXPIRING: Nothing is missing, but something lapses soon.
status_hint.NON_COMPLIANT: Something demanded is wrong. You have chosen not to refuse entry for it.
status_hint.BLOCKED: A condition you block on is not met.
status_hint.PENDING_APPROVAL: The file is with a reviewer. Nothing is missing — nobody has accepted it yet.
status_hint.SUSPENDED: Somebody suspended this file. That outranks everything computed.

rule.MISSING_MANDATORY_DOCUMENT: A mandatory document has never been supplied
rule.MISSING_RISK_ASSESSMENT: No risk assessment has been supplied
rule.MISSING_SITE_APPROVAL: No site-specific approval has been supplied
rule.INCOMPLETE_INDUCTION: A worker has not completed the site induction
rule.EXPIRED_SAFETY_FILE: The safety file approval has lapsed
rule.MISSING_MEDICAL: The work requires a certificate of fitness and none is held
rule.MISSING_METHOD_STATEMENT: The work requires a method statement and none is on file
rule.MISSING_PERMIT: The work requires a permit to work and none is open
rule.MISSING_EQUIPMENT_CERTIFICATE: The work requires an equipment certificate and none is on file

safety_file.always_blocks: always refuses, and is not switched off from here. A site decides its own gate.

activities.title: Activities
activities.subtitle: The work done on site, and what each kind takes to be allowed to do it.
activities.name: Name
activities.code_hint: What a card reader, a permit or an API sends. Upper case, no spaces.
activities.requires_hint: Credentials somebody must hold. A worker without one of these is refused for this work by name.
activities.high_risk_hint: Marks it for a second look. The gate acts on what the activity requires, not on this.
activities.permit_hint: A permit has to be open before this work may start.
activities.retire_body: It stops being offered. Permits and access events already recorded against it stay readable, and the code can be used again later.
activities.empty_body: Until an activity says what it takes, a gate asked "may this person work at height" has nothing to check against and lets everybody through. Start from the shipped South African list and change what each one requires.
activities.unstaffed: {n} activities nobody on the estate currently qualifies for. Either the certificates need chasing or the requirement is wrong.
activities.advisory_title: A missing competency is recorded, not refused
activities.advisory_body: Somebody missing a required ticket is let through and the gap is logged. Switch on "Missing competency for the activity" in the contractor blocking rules to refuse instead.

attendance.title: On site
attendance.subtitle: Who is here now, who came and went, and who never signed out.
attendance.long_stays_hint: {n} people have been on site longer than {hours} hours. Night shift looks like this too — but so does a site where nobody signs out.
attendance.search: Search by name, employer or work
attendance.when_hint: Leave empty for now. A past time is accepted, for writing up a paper list; a future one is not.
attendance.manual_note: Recorded as entered by hand, so an audit can tell it apart from a scan. A reader being down is not a reason to leave somebody off the roll-call.
attendance.everyone_in: Everybody on the roster is already signed in.
attendance.monitor_only: Would have been refused — this gate is in monitor mode.

overrides.title: Temporary access
overrides.subtitle: Who has been let past a gate they should not have been, and on whose authority.
overrides.explainer: An override admits somebody whose file is not in order. It is meant to be easy to grant — a contractor with work to do and no way through is how people end up signed in under a colleague's name — and safe because every one is listed here with its reason, its approver and its end. None may run longer than {days} days.
overrides.grant_warning: This lets somebody onto a site who would otherwise be refused. It is recorded against your name, and against the approver you name.
overrides.ending_soon_hint: {n} overrides end within two days. Renew them or let them lapse — but decide, rather than finding out at a boom.
overrides.search: Search by person, reason or approver
overrides.none_ever: No override has ever been granted.
overrides.reason_hint: What somebody reviewing this in six months has to work from. Ten characters at least.
overrides.conditions_hint: What they must do while it lasts. Printed on the gate verdict when their pass is scanned.
overrides.starts_hint: Leave empty to start now. A shutdown override can be arranged the day before.
overrides.ends_hint: Required, and at most {days} days away. It closes by itself.
overrides.site_hint: Leave empty for every site. Narrowing it is the safer choice.
overrides.approver_hint: The person who authorised it, if that is not you. Leave empty and it is recorded against you.
overrides.revoke_body: The gate goes back where it was, immediately. Anybody relying on this to get on site tomorrow will be refused.

portal.title: Your safety compliance
portal.subtitle: What {host} needs from you before your people can work on their sites.
portal.not_a_contractor: Nothing is needed from you here
portal.not_a_contractor_body: You are not on this customer's contractor register, so there are no safety requirements against your account. If your people do work on their sites, ask them to add you.
portal.score_explained: One point for each document, your safety file, and each person's induction.
portal.nothing_required: This customer has not asked you for anything yet.
portal.nothing_outstanding: Nothing outstanding. You are up to date.
portal.awaiting_review_note: Sent — waiting for them to review it
portal.no_site_decisions: No site has been decided about yet.
portal.no_workers: None of your people are on this customer's register yet.
portal.review_note: Anything you send is reviewed before it counts. It will show as waiting for review until they accept it, so do not rely on it at a gate until then.
portal.file_hint: PDF, photograph or Word document, up to 20 MB.
portal.expires_hint: Leave empty if it does not expire.
portal.upload_done: Sent. They will review it and it will count once accepted.

notices.title: Contractor notices
notices.subtitle: What this system tells your contractors, where it goes, and what actually went out.
notices.channels_hint: A small firm's registered email is often an accountant's, checked weekly. The number on the same record is usually the site manager's.
notices.none_selected: Nothing will be sent to contractors. They will find out at a gate.
notices.what_we_send_hint: Every notice this system sends a contractor, and what causes it.
notices.search: Search by contractor, message or address
notices.unreachable_body: They have no address on the channels you have chosen, so none of these notices reach them. Nothing errors — they simply go untold until somebody is turned away at a gate.

events.worker_blocked: One of their people was refused at a gate

planning.title: Procurement plans
planning.subtitle: The organisation's annual procurement requirements
planning.status_subtitle: Planned against actual, and what is running late
planning.new_plan_hint: A plan groups a financial year's requirements for one department or project.
planning.create_plan_hint: The plan starts as a draft. Add requirements before submitting it for review.
planning.no_lines: No requirements captured on this plan yet.
planning.cancel_hint: Cancelling releases any budget held against this plan's lines.
planning.no_budget_module: Budget Management is not installed, so no budget can be linked. The plan works without one.
planning.no_budget_position: No budget is linked, or Budget Management is not installed, so the financial position cannot be shown.
planning.over_budget: This plan exceeds the available budget by {amount}.
planning.budget_warning: This plan is close to the available budget.
planning.delayed_subtitle: Past the planned tender or award date and not yet awarded
planning.upcoming_subtitle: Due to go to tender within 60 days
planning.upcoming_empty: Nothing due in the next 60 days.

tenders.title: Tender reviews
tenders.subtitle: Initiation, evaluation, moderation and award recommendation
tenders.initiate_hint: A tender review carries its own committee, criteria, bids and recommendation.
tenders.create_review_hint: Criteria and committee are set up next, before evaluation opens.
tenders.plan_line_hint: Selecting a plan line carries its details across.

methodologies.WEIGHTED_hint: Every criterion weighted into one score
methodologies.TWO_ENVELOPE_hint: Technical gate first, price opened only for those who pass
methodologies.PRICE_ONLY_hint: Ranked on price among compliant bids

tenders.weights_must_total: Price and preference weights must total 100; they total {total}.
tenders.no_committees: No active committees yet — create one before evaluation can open.
tenders.approval_level_hint: Free text: the delegation level this award needs.
tenders.frozen_explainer: The criteria were frozen on {at}, when evaluation opened. A change now needs an approved criteria change request.
tenders.disqualification_reason_hint: Required. The reason appears in the recommendation report.
tenders.weight_hint: Share of 100%, or of the parent criterion.
tenders.is_mandatory: Failing this criterion disqualifies the bid
tenders.weights_problem: The criteria weights do not add up
tenders.no_evaluators: No evaluators assigned. Assign a committee first.
tenders.coi_outstanding_body: Evaluation cannot open until every voting member has declared and any declared conflict is resolved.
tenders.no_recommendation: No recommendation has been generated. Approve the scores in moderation first.
tenders.recommended_supplier_hint: Defaults to the highest ranked bid; override if the committee recommends otherwise.
tenders.submitted_at_hint: A bid received after closing is flagged as late.
tenders.jurisdiction_hint: Sets the currency and which preference rules apply.
tenders.preference_framework_hint: Fills in the statutory price and preference split.
tenders.no_framework_for_jurisdiction: No framework configured for this jurisdiction yet.
tenders.framework_unverified_warning: {name} has not been confirmed against your approved procurement policy. Check the points before awarding on them.
tenders.unconvertible_body: No exchange rate is loaded for {currencies} against {target}. Load the rate in Finance, otherwise scoring cannot rank these bids.

evaluations.title: My evaluations
evaluations.subtitle: Tenders you have been appointed to score
evaluations.none: You have no evaluations to complete
evaluations.none_hint: You will see tenders here once you are appointed to an evaluation committee.
evaluations.declare_first: Complete your conflict-of-interest declaration before scoring.
evaluations.conflict_blocked: You declared a conflict. Scoring is paused until an administrator resolves it.
evaluations.declaration_intro: Before scoring, declare whether you have any interest in a bidder on this tender.
evaluations.no_conflict: I have no conflict of interest
evaluations.have_conflict: I have a conflict of interest to declare
evaluations.confidentiality_undertaking: I accept the confidentiality undertaking for this evaluation
evaluations.conflict_pending: Your declared conflict is with an administrator. You cannot score until it is resolved.
evaluations.price_hidden: This is a two-envelope evaluation, so bid prices stay closed until the technical stage concludes.
evaluations.locked_body: Submitted {date}. This is revision {revision}. A correction needs an authorised reopening, which keeps the original scores.
evaluations.raise_concern: I have a concern about this bid
evaluations.concern_hint: Concerns are raised with the chairperson during moderation.
evaluations.submit_hint: Once submitted your scores are locked and count towards the committee score.
evaluations.confirm_submit_body: Your weighted score is {score}. After submitting, changes need an authorised reopening.

moderation.title: Moderation
moderation.subtitle: Compare the evaluators, resolve differences, approve the final scores
moderation.scores_approved: The final committee scores have been approved. A recommendation can now be generated.
moderation.open_items: {n} item(s) still open. Resolve them before approving the final scores.
moderation.variance_hint: Criteria where evaluators differ by more than {pct}% of the maximum are flagged automatically.
moderation.nothing_flagged: Nothing was flagged. Evaluators are in agreement.
moderation.no_submissions: No submitted evaluations to compare yet.
moderation.reevaluate_warning: This reopens the evaluator's submitted scores. The original scores are preserved.

committees.title: Evaluation committees
committees.subtitle: Standing committees, their members and appointments
committees.type_hint: For example bid evaluation or bid adjudication.
committees.external_hint: Someone without a platform account, appointed from outside the organisation.
committees.not_constituted: This committee is not properly constituted yet
committees.needs_quorum: It has {have} voting member(s) and its quorum is {need}.
committees.needs_external: It requires an external/independent member and has none.
committees.no_tenders: This committee has not been assigned to a tender yet.

deviations.title: Deviations
deviations.subtitle: Requests to depart from the normal procurement route
deviations.new_hint: Capture what you can now — the compliance check runs when you submit, not when you save.
deviations.motivation_hint: These are what an auditor reads first. Say what happened and why the normal route was not used.
deviations.draft_notice: Saving keeps this as a draft. The compliance rules run when you submit it for approval.
deviations.no_rules: Your organisation has not configured any compliance rules for deviations.
deviations.submit_body: The compliance rules run now, and the approval chain is selected from this deviation's value, department, type and risk.
deviations.accept_warnings: I accept these warnings and want to proceed
deviations.acceptance_reason_hint: Recorded against the check and visible to every approver.

fields.reason_hint: In one or two sentences, what makes this necessary.
fields.business_justification_hint: Why this is the right thing for the organisation to do.
fields.risk_assessment_hint: What could go wrong, and what reduces it.
fields.proposed_alternative_hint: What was considered instead, and why it was not used.
fields.financial_impact_hint: The cost of proceeding, and of not proceeding.
